build.note: This round filed thirteen entries under what_i_could_not_do before I read a line of it, including two write-ordering bugs in its own tool, an S52 invocation error, and two holes in the reference item it wrote. It then, unprompted and after filing, found the fifth null arm and rewrote its own protective ruling from a PASS to a HALF-PASS. bifurcation.side: BOTH — RI-WLD10 section 10 is explicitly bifurcated. Art direction (section 10.1 opacity, waterline on the character) judged against Morrowind; fidelity (shoreline blend against the depth buffer, refraction, foam) judged against modern references only.
bifurcation.note: RI-VIS11 declares side: modern-fidelity and REFUSES Morrowind references. I cite it on the fidelity side only.

the_headline: THE SHIPPED CHANGE IS REAL, SMALL, AND CORRECTLY DIRECTED — AND THE ROUND'S OWN INSTRUMENT WORK HAS DESTROYED THE EVIDENCE CLASS ITS ACCEPTANCE CLAUSE WAS WRITTEN IN. Three things, in order of how far they reach. (1) Threshold 16 is genuinely stable and I reproduce it on FIVE runs, two poses, five commits: the unchanged arm's own mask spreads 0.14-0.54% at threshold 16 against 28-56% at threshold 10. That is a real methodological advance over HAZARDS section 25a and it stands. But it stabilises the MASK and not PRESENCE - the presence drift band is 4.04 / 3.98 / 3.91 points at thresholds 6 / 10 / 16, identical at all three - so the threshold choice buys nothing for the round's own headline unit, and the round credits it with a stability it did not supply. (2) THE S52 NULL DOES NOT PROTECT EITHER WIDTH MEASURE, AND I DERIVED THAT FROM THE ARTIFACT BEFORE THE BUILDER'S CORRECTION REACHED ME. The null family's shore-profile span is monotone in brightness - +6.255, +3.153, +0.021, -3.06 against the arm's -7.664 - and crosses zero at almost exactly the matched point, where the tool refuses to measure below |span| 0.6. So 'no measurable transition at the matched point' is the zero-crossing of the null's own profile landing on the matched brightness: an amplitude coincidence, not an absent mechanism. At that same matched point the RAW width reads 25 against the arm's 30, and one step darker the CLOSED width reads 31 against the arm's 32, tracing the same profile shape. (3) AND THE REASON IS IN THE MEASURE'S CONSTRUCTION, WHICH SETTLES IT FOR EVERY ROUND AT ONCE: I re-implemented shoreProfile() and found gradient_width_px is EXACTLY invariant under any rescaling of luma. Compressing the shipped arm's own profile 25x toward its mean - contrast cut from 7.66 luma levels to 0.31, invisible - returns the identical 32 px. The measure records the spatial shape of whatever near-shore ordering exists and nothing about its strength. Under ARBITRATION S63's standing rule that a metric family a null reproduces is evidence in neither direction, NO width number in F7's history is admissible: not this round's 32, not round 4's 34, not round 3's 15. The `gradient_width_px >= 12` acceptance clause cannot gate a waterline and must be retired. Meanwhile the delivered state: presence rises 83.35 -> 100.16% at edge-b225 and 41.99 -> 51.38% at edge-b135, verified across two capture orders, four processes and five commits, and VISIBLE in the frames I opened. It is a strict improvement on round 4 and it is nowhere near the bar - the acceptance fails both halves, M12 now fails four sub-metrics including a newly measured TemporalVar HARD FAIL, and the round's own decomposition shows the term it was sent to fix costs 9.29 presence points where round 3's alpha multiplier costs 30.67.

job_1_the_threshold_and_whether_the_new_.verdict: CONFIRMED, on more evidence than the round claimed, WITH ONE MATERIAL QUALIFIER THE ROUND DID NOT STATE.
job_1_the_threshold_and_whether_the_new_.what_i_did: I ignored the round's tables and recomputed the drift myself from poses[].baseline_captures[].by_threshold[].own_mask_px in every banked run. Block A of my measurements file.
job_1_the_threshold_and_whether_the_new_.note_the_round_undercounted_itself: The round cites four runs, two poses, four processes. There are FIVE runs carrying baselines - it did not count dm-b135-null, whose threshold-16 spread is 0.54% and which reproduces dm-b135-verify's baselines to three decimals in a separate process at a later commit. The claim is stronger than the round made it.
job_1_the_threshold_and_whether_the_new_.the_order_reversed_control: CONFIRMED and it is the cleanest thing in the round. The identical band-0.10 arm captured 5th in the forward run and 3rd in the reverse run moves 12.52 points of own-mask at threshold 10 and 0.02 at threshold 16. HAZARDS section 25a rule 2 is satisfied and threshold 16 is order-independent as well as ordinal-independent.
job_1_the_threshold_and_whether_the_new_.THE_QUALIFIER_THE_ROUND_DID_NOT_STATE: Threshold 16 stabilises the mask and does NOT stabilise presence. baseline_drift[].presence_pct_if_scored_as_an_arm has range 4.04 / 3.98 / 3.91 points at thresholds 6 / 10 / 16 in the nine-capture run - the presence drift band is flat across thresholds. The round writes 'my threshold-16 headline is well founded for presence and for the mask, which is what I measured stability on'. Half of that is right. The presence figures survive because the effects reported (9.29 to 30.67 points) sit an order of magnitude outside a ~3.9-point band, and the round publishes the band beside every number, which is the correct discipline. But the threshold choice contributed nothing to it, and a future round must not carry 'threshold 16 is the stable threshold' forward as though it covered presence.
job_1_the_threshold_and_whether_the_new_.AND_I_CORRECT_THE_ROUND_AGAINST_ITSELF_I: The round's self-criticism says 'width stability is NOT established at any threshold' and cites 20 px vs 1 px on the unchanged arm at edge-b045. That is a comparison ACROSS thresholds, not repeat drift. Within each threshold the unchanged arm's width is flat in every run: edge-b045 reads [20,20,17,17] at threshold 10 and [1,1,1,1] at threshold 16; edge-b225 reads [1,1,1,1,1,1,1,1,1]; the published drift band is 0 px at threshold 16 in every run. So the width is REPEATABLE and threshold-conditional, not noisy. That distinction matters because it rules out capture noise as the explanation and points at the measure's construction instead - which is exactly where job 2 lands.

job_2_the_decomposition_and_whether_thre.verdict: THE DECOMPOSITION HOLDS. I re-derived it in my own arithmetic from the banked luma and it is not an assertion.
job_2_the_decomposition_and_whether_thre.how: I inferred and verified the presence formula from the artifact: presence = 100 * (L_arm - L_hidden) / (L_baseline_local - L_hidden), where L_baseline_local is the mean of the arm's two flanking baseline captures. It reproduces every published row to the digit.
job_2_the_decomposition_and_whether_thre.so_the_answer_to_the_orchestrators_quest: YES. Three rounds of shore-band work have been arguing about a term worth 9.29 presence points while a multiplier nobody was sent at costs 30.67. The round's ruling that round 6 should attack `diffuseColor.a * 0.42` at water.js:320 is supported by its own numbers and by mine, and it is visible: the no-shorefade frame reads as water with a bed visible through it and the shipped frame reads as mud.
job_2_the_decomposition_and_whether_thre.THE_CEILING_NOBODY_HAS_STATED_AND_IT_BOU: Deleting the shore alpha term ENTIRELY scores 91.34% at this pose, against a 90% bar with a 3.75-point drift band at this pose. A total removal of the multiplier clears the acceptance by 1.34 points inside a 3.75-point band - i.e. not distinguishably. A round 6 that removes the multiplier and nothing else should NOT be expected to pass clause 2 at edge-b135. The remaining ~8.7 points are the depth colour itself, which no round has been sent at. If the 90% bar is to be met at this pose, the multiplier is necessary and is not sufficient, and that should be in the round-6 brief.
job_2_the_decomposition_and_whether_thre.the_band_change_verified_before_shipping: CONFIRMED from the artifacts. At edge-b225, threshold 16: r3 100.21, band-0.05 100.41, band-0.10 100.35, band-0.20 100.10, band-0.30 99.57, band-0.60 96.59, fixed(1.20) 83.35 - a 17.0-point gap to the shipped default at identical width. The round is correct and admirably careful that band-0.30 and band-0.60 sit INSIDE the 96.09-100 drift band and are not distinguishable from an arm that changed nothing; only 1.20 m sits outside. The choice of 0.10 over 0.05 or 0.20 rests on the offline census, not on captures, and the round says so.
job_2_the_decomposition_and_whether_thre.the_before_and_after: The tidiest reversal proof in the piece. `fixed` means the source default, so the forward run measured it at 1.20 m and the reverse run, launched after the change landed, measured it at 0.10 m: same arm name, same pose, same threshold, same tool - presence 83.35 -> 100.16%. Two rows differing by one number in one file. I checked the commits differ (5e91b7eb vs df9ec7b4) and that water.js:132 now reads 0.10.
job_2_the_decomposition_and_whether_thre.the_acceptance: FAILS BOTH HALVES AND THE ROUND DOES NOT CLAIM IT. Presence at the complete Deep Marshes 4-set on the shipped arm, threshold 16: 100.17 / 51.38 / 100.35 / 100.62 - worst pose 51.38 against a 90% bar. Width: 1 / 32 / 1 / 3 - worst pose 1 px against a 12 px bar. I reproduce all eight figures from the banked artifacts.

job_3_the_three_debts_and_the_null_that_.motion: PAID, and it is the first motion in five rounds. 12-bearing orbits with phase live, 58 frames banked, two arms. I opened four of them. The water at orbit bearing 255 reads as a flat teal sheet with hard polygonal facet edges and heavy speckle - no ripple, no specular, no waterline. That is RI-VIS04 section 9's TELL almost word for word.
job_3_the_three_debts_and_the_null_that_.temporalvar: CONFIRMED AS A HARD FAIL, and I re-derived it rather than reading it. node tools/visual/f7-r5-offline.mjs --mode temporal returns 0.000341 against a 0.0005 hard-fail floor, from a separate invocation. I ran the identity check myself: md5sum over the 30 temporal frames returns 30 distinct hashes, so HAZARDS section 30's trap is ruled out. The land control (0.000256) and the per-pixel controls (water 0.000525, land 0.000107) agree.
job_3_the_three_debts_and_the_null_that_.the_limit_on_it: The 30-frame sequence was shot on the arm named `fixed` at commit 5e91b7eb, where `fixed` was still 1.20 m. The shipped 0.10 m arm has only 2 temporal frames, below the >= 5 the tool itself requires. TemporalVar has not been measured on the configuration this round ships. It is very unlikely to differ and I do not treat it as a defect in the finding, but the round reports the number without naming the arm and a future round should not inherit it as 'the shipped arm's'.
job_3_the_three_debts_and_the_null_that_.supersample: CONFIRMED. 64.95% high-frequency survival on the shipped arm and 64.01% on round 2's, against an 84.77% / 85.85% land control, is in the banked artifact (the supersample run is post-fix and its numbers ARE in sweep.json, unlike the motion run's). Under RI-VIS11 section 3 that is `unresolved`, fails closed, and NormalEnergy - the one M12 sub-metric F7 has been passing for three rounds - is no longer admissible as a pass. Both arms read the same, so this is a standing property of our water and not something a recent round caused.
job_3_the_three_debts_and_the_null_that_.THE_S52_NULL: HALF-PASS AT BEST, AND ON MY READING IT PROTECTS NOTHING. I derived this from the banked artifact BEFORE the orchestrator's correction reached me, by opening dm-b135-null/sweep.json and finding null-t0.90 present with full metrics and a frame on disk, in the same commit (d597e2cd) whose message reads 'S52 matched null passes' and whose status edit says null-t0.90 'did not capture'. The builder has since found the same thing itself and rewritten the ruling, which I credit.
job_3_the_three_debts_and_the_null_that_.and_i_go_one_step_further_than_the_build: The builder's correction says the closed width is 'protected at the arm's brightness but not brightness-proof in general'. I do not think it is protected at all. The null family's closed-profile span at threshold 16 runs +6.255, +3.153, +0.021, -3.06 against the arm's -7.664 - monotone in brightness, crossing zero at almost exactly the matched point. The tool refuses to measure when |span| < 0.6/255. So the protective result is the zero-crossing of the null's OWN profile landing on the matched brightness. It is an amplitude coincidence. And the profiles are the same shape: band-0.10 rises 50.8 -> 63.5 by distance bin 6 then falls to 47 by bin 24; null-t0.90 - no depth dependence, no k, no shore geometry - rises 45.1 -> 51.9 by bin 6 then falls to 47.2 by bin 24. The arm and a brightness-only null trace the same curve at different amplitudes.
job_3_the_three_debts_and_the_null_that_.the_construction_that_settles_it: I re-implemented shoreProfile() from tools/visual/f7-r5-sweep.mjs:155-178 and tested it. gradient_width_px is EXACTLY invariant under any affine rescaling of the luma profile - it is d90 minus d10 on a span-normalised curve, with the only amplitude gate being the |span| >= 0.6 refusal. I ran the shipped arm's own banked profile through my re-implementation and got its published 32 px; I then compressed the same profile 10x and 25x toward its mean - contrast cut from 7.66 luma levels to 0.77 and 0.31, well below anything a player could see - and got 32 px both times. The measure records the spatial shape of whatever near-shore ordering exists and nothing about its strength.
which_explains_every_width_anomaly_in_th: null-t0.90 reads 31 against the arm's 32 with 40% of the contrast, because contrast is not what it measures.
The round's unexplained r3 closed-vs-raw split (closed 1, raw 30) is two masks giving two profile shapes, not noise.
The edge-b045 20-vs-1 threshold swing is the same thing - which is why block A finds the width perfectly repeatable WITHIN each threshold.

job_4_does_RI_VIS11_earn_its_place.verdict: YES. It earns its place, it survives the section 1.3 guards, and its central claim reproduces in my own run. It has one stale citation and its thresholds are first-draft, both of which it declares.
job_4_does_RI_VIS11_earn_its_place.i_reproduced_section_1_and_2_rather_than: node tools/visual/f7-r5-offline.mjs --mode stipple over round 4's banked dm-edge2 frames returns water phase_spread_lsb 0.5281 (fixed) and 0.6127 (prefix) against land controls of 1.2784 and 1.1436, and adjacent/two-apart energies of 6.167/6.663 and 7.173/7.832 against land 9.638/13.172. Every figure in the item's tables reproduces to the digit from a separate invocation.
job_4_does_RI_VIS11_earn_its_place.so_the_falsification_is_real: The 4x4 phase signature on our water is under two thirds of an 8-bit level and is two to five times LARGER on the land the water shader never touches. There is no ordered dither. Four consecutive critics named one and handed the name on, and this is exactly the inherited-figure failure the project keeps finding, caught by someone finally measuring it. That is worth the item on its own.

the_section_1_3_guards.ADD_only: SATISFIED. RI-VIS11 relaxes no existing threshold. It ADDS a gate on NormalEnergy (a pass only where hf_survival >= 70%) and adds a phase_spread_lsb >= 2.0 fail that would catch a real dither if one appeared. Net effect on the corpus is strictly tighter.
the_section_1_3_guards.a_bar_the_author_wrote_may_not_be_why_it: SATISFIED, and in the strongest possible direction. The first measurement ever taken against RI-VIS11 section 3 returns 64.95% - `unresolved`, fails closed - and its effect is to REMOVE the only M12 sub-metric F7 has been passing. The author wrote a bar and then failed itself on it. That is section 1.3 working exactly as the 2026-08-15 correction intends.
the_section_1_3_guards.the_one_place_it_cuts_the_authors_way: Section 1 retires the 'dither' diagnosis, which removes a criticism from F7's ledger. I therefore did not accept it - I re-ran the instrument myself and it reproduces. And it is retired only to be replaced by a worse finding (aliasing-class, unresolved, NormalEnergy gated off), so nothing passes because of it.

the_two_holes_the_round_declared.the_undefined_middle_band: HANDLED CORRECTLY. The first draft banded >= 70% and hard-failed < 45% and said nothing between; the first number taken landed at 64.95%. The round amended the item the same turn to make 45-70% `unresolved`, failing closed, citing ARBITRATION S61's asymmetry, and recorded the hole in the item's own text with a dated note. The alternative - rounding 64.95 into whichever neighbouring verdict was convenient - is the failure mode this repo is full of. This is the right handling and I would not mark it down.
the_two_holes_the_round_declared.the_missing_land_control: HANDLED CORRECTLY AND DECLARED. The in-browser supersample mode produced the water half without the land half the item itself requires, so the row was made admissible by computing the control offline from the banked frames rather than by publishing it anyway. The item's own text records the sequence. An item whose first use exposed two holes in it is an item being used properly.

job_4_does_RI_VIS11_earn_its_place.the_defect_i_found: RI-VIS11 section 2 cites water.js 'lines 304-306' for the three procedural terms at 4.7 / 13.7 / 26.3 radians per world metre. Read this turn, those terms are at lines 323-325; line 304 is inside the shore-band comment block. The frequencies are exactly right - the citation went stale within the round when the shore-band edit landed above them. One-line fix, and worth making, because stale citations have bitten this repo three times.
job_4_does_RI_VIS11_earn_its_place.and_the_ablation_it_owes: The round declares it did not ablate the three terms and sets confidence: medium accordingly, per ARBITRATION S63. Correct. See my own candidate mechanism below, which I also did not ablate and also do not claim.

job_5_the_self_filed_defects_and_whether.verdict: ONE PUBLISHED NUMBER IS DOWNSTREAM OF THE UNFIXED WINDOW, AND THE ROUND'S MITIGATION HOLDS IT UP.
job_5_the_self_filed_defects_and_whether.the_write_ordering_bugs: CONFIRMED AS REAL AND CONFIRMED AS COSTLY IN ONE PLACE. dm-motion/sweep.json has `motion: {}` - the entire motion block is absent from the banked artifact, because that run was captured at commit 5e91b7eb with the pre-fix tool. So every motion number in the status (TemporalVar, the orbit coverage, the mean_Yp series) came from the console log, not the artifact. HAZARDS section 18's exact shape, and round 4's own criticism repeated.
job_5_the_self_filed_defects_and_whether.why_it_does_not_sink_the_finding: The round anticipated it and moved TemporalVar into an offline tool that recomputes from the banked PNGs. I ran that tool and got 0.000341 from a separate invocation, and the 58 frames are on disk. So the number is recoverable and I confirm it. The mean_Yp series and the orbit frame list are NOT recoverable from the artifact and exist only in the log - a minor loss, but a critic should know the motion block is empty before citing it.
job_5_the_self_filed_defects_and_whether.the_supersample_run_is_clean: dm-supersample/sweep.json was captured at commit 362e569c with the fixed tool and its numbers ARE in the artifact. I verified the fix in source: both branches now assign out.supersample[poseId] / out.motion[poseId] BEFORE the arm loop.
job_5_the_self_filed_defects_and_whether.the_S52_invocation_error: CONFIRMED as declared - arms defined via --nulls and not included in the explicit --arms list, so they were never captured, found by reading the output table rather than before launching. The round is right that this nearly cost it the protection. What it cost instead was subtler and worse: the replacement run finished so close to filing that the round wrote its ruling from the log while committing an artifact that contradicted it.
job_5_the_self_filed_defects_and_whether.THE_ONE_I_WOULD_ADD: The status file still carries an internal contradiction. Its top-level `a_note_on_the_last_two_runs` says null-t0.90 'is the one arm that did not capture'; its job-2 S52 block, corrected later, tabulates null-t0.90's full results at both thresholds. Both sentences are in the file at the commit I read. The corrected block is right. The header should be fixed so the next reader does not inherit the wrong one - this is precisely how a false figure travels.

bar_findings.finding: THE `gradient_width_px >= 12` ACCEPTANCE CLAUSE CANNOT GATE AND MUST BE RETIRED. This is the orchestrator's clause, written into the round-4 brief, and the orchestrator asked me to rule on it.
bar_findings.the_evidence: gradient_width_px is exactly invariant under any rescaling of the luma profile - I re-implemented the measure, reproduced the shipped arm's published 32 px, then compressed the same profile 25x toward its mean (contrast 7.66 -> 0.31 luma levels) and got 32 px again. It records the spatial shape of whatever near-shore ordering exists and nothing about its strength. A brightness-only null with no depth dependence, no k and no shore geometry reproduces 25 of the arm's 30 raw px at matched luminance and 31 of its 32 closed px one step darker, tracing the same profile curve.
bar_findings.the_ruling: Under ARBITRATION S63's standing rule - a metric family a null reproduces is evidence in neither direction - NO width number in F7's history is admissible. Not this round's 32, not round 4's 34, not round 3's 15. The clause should be struck from the round-6 acceptance rather than carried forward.
bar_findings.what_replaces_it_and_this_is_an_ADD_not_: Two clauses, neither of which a dimmer can satisfy. (1) PRESENCE, which the round has now established is threshold-independent (spread 0.17-0.59 points across four thresholds on nine arms), carries a published interleaved drift band, and has a real control behind it. (2) A CONTRAST clause on the waterline itself: publish |span| - the near-shore-to-open-water luma difference the width measure currently discards - and require it to exceed the unchanged arm's own drift band by a stated margin AND to have the expected sign. |span| is NOT scale-invariant, so a matched-luminance null CAN falsify it, which is exactly what the width measure cannot do. Width may still be reported, but only conditional on the contrast clause passing first, and never as a gate on its own.
bar_findings.the_guard_i_am_bound_by: CRITIC-DOCTRINE section 1.3: I may only ADD, and a clause I write may never be the reason anything passes. This replacement fails the round-5 build too - presence 51.38% at the worst pose against a 90% bar, and the contrast clause is unmeasured because no round has published |span| as a gated quantity. I am not rescuing anything with it. It is offered for the round-6 acceptance and I have not applied it to this score, which rests on the existing bar.
bar_findings.who_should_write_it: It belongs in RI-VIS03 M12 beside M12a, as an ADD by whoever writes the round-6 brief. I did not write it into the corpus myself: per section 1.3's third guard this is a piece of instrument work rather than a hole I can close inside a critique, and doing it properly needs the drift measurement for |span| across a pose set that nobody has run.
bar_findings.reversible: Overturned if someone shows a matched-luminance null that reproduces |span| as well - in which case the contrast clause is in the dimmer family too and the whole shoreline claim needs a different instrument.

A CANDIDATE MECHANISM FOR THE TEMPORALVAR HARD FAIL THAT I DID NOT ABLATE AND DO NOT CLAIM. Read this turn at water.js:323-328, the three ripple terms are added to outgoingLight with coefficients of order 0.010 multiplied by a (term - .5) spanning +/-0.5, so peak combined luma contribution is of order 0.008 against water whose mean Yp is 0.180 - roughly a 0.5-1% modulation, living entirely at the 4.7 / 13.7 / 26.3 rad-per-metre frequencies RI-VIS11 shows collapse under supersampling. If that holds, the M12 TemporalVar hard fail and the RI-VIS11 aliasing finding are two halves of one defect in three lines of source: the ripple is simultaneously too small to move the mean and too high-frequency to survive a resolve. Per ARBITRATION S63 I may not narrate a mechanism I did not ablate, so this is a candidate with its arithmetic shown, NOT a finding. One browser run settles it: scale the three coefficients up and the three frequencies down, and re-measure TemporalVar and hf_survival together.

what_would_make_this_verdict_wrong: If gradient_width_px is not the measure I re-implemented - i.e. if I mis-read shoreProfile() and the real measure has an amplitude term I missed. That would overturn my biggest_gap. The test is cheap: anyone can run my re-implementation against a banked profile and check it returns the published number, which it does.

RESOLVED, and it had pointed against me. Every null arm records edits_applied 10 against edits_expected 2, which on its face suggests the shader edit did something other than advertised - and if so the null is not a null and my S52 finding collapses. Reading applyShaderArm() at f7-r5-sweep.mjs:375-388: edits_expected is edits.length (the two replacements), while __R5_EDITS increments once per matched needle per material recompile across the 11 water materials, so 10 is ~5 recompiled materials x 2 needles rather than 10 distinct edits. Line 598 confirms the intended reading - a ZERO count is what marks an arm VACUOUS. And the arms' mean luma moves 8-25 levels, which cannot happen unless the edit reached the compiled shader. The nulls applied and the finding stands.

If my FresnelDelta correction is a threshold artefact - the M12 sub-metrics are computed over the pinned mask and the mask changes with threshold, so a worst-pose value at threshold 16 is not directly comparable to one at threshold 6. I report both and the conclusion (M12's two-or-more clause met) does not depend on it.

If the Western Rootlands, at 1 of 4 bearings, would change the min-over-poses picture. It can only make it worse - the round measured 69.35% presence there at round 4's value - but I cannot say by how much and no score here rests on it.

If a blind judge, seeing the frames, ranked the shipped arm above the no-shorefade arm. My reading that one looks like water and the other looks like mud is an unchecked look claim and it is the one thing in this verdict a fresh pair of eyes could simply overturn.

notes: Three things a round-6 brief must carry, and none of them is 'tune the band'. (1) The width gate is retired and replaced before any build is dispatched, or round 6 will produce a number that cannot be read. (2) The multiplier at water.js:320 is the target, and removing it entirely reaches 91.34% at the failing pose against a 90% bar with a 3.75-point band - necessary, not sufficient, and the brief must say so rather than promise a pass. (3) TemporalVar and hf_survival should be attacked together in one ablation of water.js:323-325, because they may be one defect. The Western Rootlands owes three bearings and the blind gate owes everything.
